title: priv-installer: HA & DR automation (multi-AZ helm, terraform, upgrade/rollback, runbooks-as-code)
author: Ava Morgan
release_notes: Added HA/DR automation for Private deployments: multi-AZ helm defaults, Terraform networking module improvements, installer upgrade/rollback tooling, and runbooks-as-code for restore/failover drills.
description:
Motivation: Private (VPC/on-prem) customers have asked for automated high-availability and disaster-recovery runbooks and tooling that can be exercised as part of routine drills and during upgrades. This PR bundles changes to the installer, Helm charts, Terraform modules, and runbook-as-code to provide a repeatable HA/DR automation flow.

Summary of changes (single-string description): This PR: 1) updates the private Helm chart defaults to support multi-AZ topologies (replica counts, anti-affinity, topologySpreadConstraints, PDBs), 2) adds a Terraform networking module to create multi-AZ route/NAT / cross-AZ peering patterns and optional multi-AZ ELB placements, 3) implements upgrade and rollback automation in the installer CLI (preflight checks, canary rollout, health-check driven automatic rollback), 4) adds restore/failover drill automation (runbooks-as-code YAML + runner scripts) that orchestrate snapshot restore, DNS failover, and service validation, and 5) includes integration tests and docs.

Checklist:
- [x] Helm: topology aware defaults + migration note to values-az.yaml
- [x] Terraform: networking module + example usage
- [x] Installer: upgrade/rollback automation + new CLI flags (--drill, --force-failover)
- [x] Runbooks: ha-drill and restore-playbook as code under runbooks/drills
- [x] Tests: integration test for restore drill + e2e smoke for canary rollout
- [x] Docs: README updates and runbook docs

Design/Details: Helm changes include a new optional values file values-az.yaml which toggles multi-AZ aware settings (podAntiAffinity: requiredDuringScheduling, topologySpreadConstraints keyed to topology.kubernetes.io/zone, increased default replica counts for stateful components, and explicit leader-election pod priorities). POD Disruption Budgets are tuned to allow safe maintenance windows.

Terraform: new module terraform/modules/networking supports provisioning cross-AZ route tables, nat gateways optionally per-AZ (configurable), and an outputs map for subnet-to-az mapping used by installer templates. We keep backward compatibility by defaulting to single-AZ behavior unless multi_az = true. Example usage is under examples/multi-az/README.md.

Installer: added upgrade_tool.go and a CLI subcommand `priv-installer upgrade` with flags: --canary-percent, --drill, --rollback-on-failure, and --dry-run. The upgrade flow runs preflight checks (k8s readiness, KV cache size, backlog), performs canary rollout to a subset of nodes, runs health probes and latency smoke tests, and either completes or triggers an automated rollback path which restores previous image + re-applies last-known-good routing. Rollback path uses snapshot state (S3-compatible storage) and executes the runbook steps if a restore is required.

Runbooks-as-code: added runbooks/drills/ha-drill-2026-02.yaml and restore-playbook-automated.yaml. The runbooks are consumable by the new runbook-runner (scripts/runbook-runner.sh) which sequences steps, runs checks and emits structured events for the Console. Runbook steps are intentionally idempotent and include timeouts and escalation hooks.

Testing: added tests/restore_drill_integration_test.go and tests/canary_rollout_smoke_test.go. CI runs these as part of the private-installer integration pipeline behind a feature flag. One integration test was flaky in the first run; it was rerun and passed.

Changed areas/files (high-level): see changed_files list included in PR metadata.

Commits (high-level):
- feat(helm): multi-az defaults + values-az.yaml template
- feat(terraform): add networking module + examples
- feat(installer): add upgrade tool and rollback automation
- feat(runbooks): add ha-drill and restore-playbook as code
- test: add integration tests for restore drill and canary rollout
- docs: update README and runbook docs

Review notes and migration guidance: Customers must opt into multi-AZ behavior by supplying values-az.yaml or setting multi_az = true in Terraform. Migration doc included under docs/migration/multi-az.md. Backwards compatibility preserved for single-AZ.

Related: builds on prior runbooks updates PRs pr-2751 and pr-846 and links to Linear ENG-4271 and ENG-4310 for automation scope.

CI and merge: CI: unit/lint passed; integration had one flaky test -> rerun -> pass. Merge method: squash and merge.

review_comments: Maya Patel (reviewer): Please add a migration note for operators running single-AZ clusters. Response: added docs/migration/multi-az.md and values-az.example.yaml.
Ethan Zhang (reviewer): Suggest lowering default canary percent to 10% and add explicit health-check timeouts. Response: lowered default canary to 10% and added probe timeouts in upgrade_tool.go.
Luis Romero (SRE): Can the runbook runner emit structured events for the Console? Response: added telemetry/emit_runbook_events.go and a small JSON events schema (kept minimal to avoid coupling).
Priya Shah (security): Ensure snapshots to object storage encrypt with KMS. Response: installer now validates s3 encryption flag and KMS key presence during preflight.

Announce runbook automation in private-installer release notes and support channels
Monitor canary rollouts for first 72 hours after rollout
